title: Bagging, Blending & Stacking
interviewAnswer: Ensembling combines diverse models to reduce error. Bagging averages models trained on resampled data; stacking learns a meta-model from out-of-fold predictions; blending uses a held-out set.
why: Bagging, Blending & Stacking is a standard part of a broad data/ML curriculum because it changes how models are selected, evaluated or operated in real systems.
deepDive: Ensembling combines diverse models to reduce error. Bagging averages models trained on resampled data; stacking learns a meta-model from out-of-fold predictions; blending uses a held-out set. Stacking needs leakage-safe out-of-fold predictions. Complex ensembles cost latency/maintenance. A strong answer connects the formal idea to validation, data requirements and failure modes instead of treating the method as a recipe.
workedExample: Stack a linear model and gradient-boosted trees using out-of-fold predictions as meta-features.
commonMistakes: Choosing the technique without checking whether its assumptions match the problem.
Optimizing an offline metric without checking realistic validation slices or operational constraints.
followUps: When would you not use Bagging, Blending & Stacking?
How would you validate or tune Bagging, Blending & Stacking?
production: In production, validate on realistic slices, track latency/cost when relevant, and monitor for distribution changes or failure modes that the offline metric can hide.
